scores.accuracy_concern: NICE NG97 supports lowest dose for shortest time and reassessment at least every 6 weeks, but the week 1 to 2 checks and the week 12 checkpoint are the post's own structure and must be labelled as suggested practice, not guidance; the Cochrane withdrawal review (Van Leeuwen 2018) is low certainty and mostly excludes people with severe symptoms, so 'can be withdrawn without worsening' needs that qualifier.
scores.sharpen: Separate it clearly from C08-07 and C08-17 by making it the drug-chart version: a one-line template (target symptom, dose, review date, plan to stop) that a prescriber can copy.

scores.values_concern: Avoid presenting living alone with dementia as inherently unsafe; outcome evidence is mixed and many people choose it.
scores.accuracy_concern: The Eichler 2016 figures (51% living alone, 9% with no carer) come from a German primary care cohort and need checking in full text; do not generalise them to the UK without a UK figure; the Miranda-Castillo unmet-needs claim is unverified.
scores.sharpen: Lead with a verified figure for how often dementia trials require a study partner, then give the single test question for any service plan: who does this step if nobody else lives there?

scores.accuracy_concern: The care home finding comes from secondary and post hoc analyses, and 'roughly doubled the risk' turns a hazard ratio (2.09) into a times-more-likely statement, which house rules forbid; give the absolute proportions moved to a care home in year 1 by arm if the paper reports them, and state that the trial was in community-dwelling people with moderate to severe Alzheimer's disease.
scores.sharpen: Replace the hazard ratio with absolute numbers per group moved to a care home in the first year, and add one line on when stopping is clearly right (intolerable side effects, slow pulse or faints, last weeks of life).

scores.accuracy_concern: The five-stage meal model is a teaching synthesis, not a validated staging; the claim that swallowing problems predominate in later stages has no located source (Kai 2015 not found); the post must not imply that swallow referral is wrong when there is coughing, choking or chest infection.
scores.sharpen: Add one explicit line on when a swallow assessment is still needed (coughing, choking, wet voice, chest infections), so watching the meal reads as the first step rather than a substitute for dysphagia assessment.

scores.accuracy_concern: Figures must come from the corrected version (2020 corrigendum); the 'gain' line that life after diagnosis depends on things people can work on is a causal reading of correlational data; the draft opening has an unverified N and no reader action.
scores.sharpen: Open on the concrete finding that memory scores had only a weak link with quality of life, and close with one supportable action, such as asking for mood and physical health to be reviewed at follow-up, not only memory.

scores.accuracy_concern: Goal attainment was rated by participants and carers who knew their allocation, and therapy directly targeted those goals, so a large gain on them with no change on general scales is partly expected; state this rather than implying the standard scales failed; verify the d values (0.97, 0.94) and who rated them.
scores.sharpen: Name two verified goal types from the trial and add one sentence on why self-rated goals in an unblinded trial need cautious reading; that makes the 'what gets counted' argument more credible, not less.

scores.accuracy_concern: Schneider 2005 gives 3.5% vs 2.3% deaths (about 1 extra in 100 over 10 to 12 weeks) in trial populations that differ from many people treated in practice; a verified absolute benefit figure is hard to derive from standardised effect sizes, so the icon array must not imply a measured benefit count; the stroke claim needs a specific source.
scores.sharpen: If no absolute benefit figure can be verified, describe benefit in words (small on average, some people clearly better), keep the icon array to deaths only, and end on the two questions families can ask.

scores.accuracy_concern: Gill 2009 is observational with possible confounding by indication; rates are per 1000 person-years and must be translated accurately; confirm the age range of the Ontario cohort; the hip fracture association must not be written as caused by the drug.
scores.sharpen: Frame the pulse check as a question to ask at review ('Has anyone checked the pulse since the tablet started?') and credit the SmPC for the pharmacology, keeping the cohort data as a link, not a cause.

scores.values_concern: Harrison 2017 is co-authored by Alasdair: cite its published findings only and never present it as his work or opinion; present care homes neutrally, as the right place for some people, not as failure.
scores.accuracy_concern: Harrison 2017 describes 100 people in one Scottish setting (verify); the claim that discharge guidance advises against long-term care decisions from acute beds needs an opened official document; the legal principles differ between England and Wales (MCA 2005) and Scotland (AWI 2000) and must be stated separately.
scores.sharpen: Use the verified finding that there were no established standards for these decisions, and close with a specific request: ask whether the long-term decision can wait until after the acute stay.

scores.accuracy_concern: Observational with plausible reverse causation (people with more complex needs see more GPs); the incontinence (OR 0.42) and admission (OR 0.90) results are odds ratios and must not become 'X times less likely'; the claim that practices rarely measure continuity has no source; in England every patient already has a named accountable GP, so the request should be to see the same GP.
scores.sharpen: Change the family action to 'ask to book with the same GP each time and keep a note of who you saw', and lead the visual with the absolute medicine counts rather than the odds ratios.

scores.accuracy_concern: The IMCA duty applies to serious medical treatment and long-term accommodation (hospital stays over 28 days, care home stays over 8 weeks) in England and Wales only; the Scottish s259 right of access to advocacy is not a duty to instruct for specific decisions; drop the variation-in-rates claim unless sourced.
scores.sharpen: Open on the practical trigger (nobody to consult, not counting paid carers) and add the accommodation time thresholds so staff know when the duty starts.

scores.accuracy_concern: The direction of the self versus proxy difference needs confirming in full text; in advanced dementia self-report is often not possible, so proxies are sometimes the only option; note the tension with C08-26, whose WHELD primary outcome was proxy-rated.
scores.sharpen: Give one verified direction-and-size finding and a concrete rule (report self and proxy ratings separately, never merge them) so the post ends on an instruction, not only a critique.

scores.accuracy_concern: The final core outcome set (Reilly 2020) was not found, so only the Harding 2019 long-list domains are verified; the contrast claim that services report mainly activity measures needs a source.
scores.sharpen: Either verify the final core outcome set and name two specific items, or fold the neighbourhood-and-home point into C08-06 or C08-12 as supporting material.

scores.accuracy_concern: Evidence is not dementia-specific; the NHS Discharge Medicines Service is England only and its page could not be opened; Nazar 2016 is observational and its readmission finding needs checking; Scotland and Wales have different arrangements.
scores.sharpen: Anchor it in a verified figure on medicine discrepancies after discharge in older people, keep the two exact questions, and say the pharmacy referral route differs by nation.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 7 vs 1 deaths was a post hoc comparison with p = 0.065 and small numbers, so it must read as uncertain, not as a proven harm; the claim that falls in antipsychotic prescribing come with rises in other sedating drugs needs its own source or should be cut; confirm the care setting of SYMBAD participants.
scores.sharpen: Keep the mortality panel but give the plain reading ('too few deaths to be sure, and no benefit to set against them'), and either source the substitution pattern or drop it.

scores.accuracy_concern: The Cochrane certainty grading must be quoted exactly; the NICE recommendation covers mild to moderate depression in mild to moderate dementia only, so the post must not imply antidepressants are never appropriate, for example in severe depression or a pre-existing mental illness.
scores.sharpen: Separate it from C08-15 by leading on the NICE recommendation and a verified non-drug first step, and state where an antidepressant may still be reasonable.

scores.accuracy_concern: McKeith 1992 is a small, older study, so give its sensitivity reaction frequency exactly or describe it in words; the four-question checklist is a prompt, not a validated screen, and hallucinations and parkinsonism also occur in other dementias; NICE allows cautious antipsychotic use in Lewy body disease with specialist input.
scores.sharpen: Keep the dream-enactment opening and word the footer as 'any yes: consider Lewy body disease and seek specialist advice before an antipsychotic', quoting the NICE caution exactly.

scores.accuracy_concern: The 2023 Cochrane review gives lower certainty for quality of life than for cognition, so 'benefits for thinking and quality of life' needs qualifying; availability varies by area and 'often available' needs a source or should be dropped.
scores.sharpen: State the size of the cognitive benefit in plain words, give the programme format from Spector 2003 (14 sessions over 7 weeks), and say plainly that access varies by area.

scores.accuracy_concern: DVLA and gov.uk pages could not be opened here, so the legal duty and the fine amount need an opened official document or a published paper; Northern Ireland uses the DVA; Chihuri 2016 pools observational studies, so the depression figure is a link, not a cause.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the less-known facts (a diagnosis does not always mean stopping at once; the insurer must also be told) and make the 'list the trips that count and how each will happen' plan the centre of the visual.

scores.values_concern: Keep to eligibility facts and avoid implying any view on benefits policy.
scores.accuracy_concern: In Scotland, Pension Age Disability Payment has replaced Attendance Allowance for new claims, so a 'Great Britain' framing is wrong for Scottish readers; gov.uk pages could not be opened and rates change each April; the severe mental impairment disregard needs a doctor's certificate plus a qualifying benefit, and the 25% discount applies only in particular household situations.
scores.sharpen: Build it on primary legislation (Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992 s64; Local Government Finance Act 1992 Sch 1) with separate lines for England and Wales and for Scotland, and leave out weekly rates.

scores.values_concern: Avoid framing walking outdoors as behaviour to be stopped; support the person's freedom to go out as well as preparation.
scores.accuracy_concern: The 'no 24-hour rule' needs an opened police document or a published source; the figures (281 incidents, 5% significant harm, 0.5% of the regional dementia population) must be checked against Bantry White and Montgomery 2015, which covers one UK region; check whether guidance says 999 or 101.
scores.sharpen: Keep the myth-correction opening, bring 'most people are found unharmed' forward to avoid alarm, and name the Herbert Protocol with a note that local names differ.

scores.values_concern: Describe advanced dementia as a terminal illness alongside the care that continues (comfort, company, symptom relief), so it does not read as withdrawal of care.
scores.accuracy_concern: The adjusted OR 0.12 is an association in a US nursing home cohort; the angle's 'knowing what to expect changed the care people received' is causal and must become 'was linked with'; UK applicability must be stated.
scores.sharpen: Open on the verified eating-problem probability (about 86 in 100 over 18 months) and close with the question families can ask: what do you expect to happen next, and what will you offer when it does?

scores.values_concern: Make clear that careful hand feeding continues care and nutrition, and that the question is the likely benefit of the tube, not the person's worth.
scores.accuracy_concern: The evidence is observational (no randomised trials), so 'has not been shown' is correct and 'no benefit' would not be; cite the current Cochrane version; the AGS statement is US, and the current UK RCP guidance wording needs checking.
scores.sharpen: Separate it from C08-22 by focusing on the single decision at the hospital moment, and add the sourced burdens (restraint, displacement, hospital visits) to the comparison card.

scores.values_concern: Guard against the null cognition result reading as a reason not to offer exercise to people with dementia.
scores.accuracy_concern: Check that DAPA is the 'largest UK' trial before saying so; the 1.4-point ADAS-cog difference should be read as no benefit and possibly slight harm, not proven harm; the secondary outcomes need verifying.
scores.sharpen: Say 'a large UK trial' unless 'largest' is verified, and close with a positive instruction: offer exercise for strength, balance and enjoyment, with a named way to find a programme.

scores.accuracy_concern: The review covers structured music-based interventions of at least five sessions, mostly in institutions, so it does not describe casual listening at home; certainty levels must be quoted exactly from the 2025 update.
scores.sharpen: Add one line on what was tested (structured sessions, mostly in care homes) so readers do not apply it to the radio, and end with how to use music for enjoyment and mood.

scores.accuracy_concern: Effect sizes (0.23 to 0.30) are small and quality of life was proxy-rated (DEMQOL-Proxy); about a third of randomised residents did not complete 9 months; verify the cost result and its uncertainty.
scores.sharpen: Translate the small effect sizes into plain words and name the one component most homes could start with, so managers get a first step, not only a trial summary.

scores.values_concern: Deception in dementia care is ethically contested; mark the position as judgement and keep the person's dignity central without licensing convenience lies.
scores.accuracy_concern: The inquiry's range of responses and its recommendations must be quoted from the Mental Health Foundation 2016 report itself; the claim that repeated news of a death causes fresh grief needs a source.
scores.sharpen: Keep the opening question and make the test 'what would help this person now?' the centre of the visual, with one clearly labelled illustrative example of answering the feeling behind the question.

scores.accuracy_concern: A single US study of 89 residents in six Maryland nursing homes; unmet needs were assessed by researchers and are associated with behaviour, not proven causes; the claim about time without activity needs a source.
scores.sharpen: Add the scale of the finding (about three unmet needs per resident) and state explicitly that this question comes after physical causes are checked, then give the care-plan question.

scores.values_concern: Must not imply a position on NICE or NHS funding decisions about anti-amyloid drugs.
scores.accuracy_concern: The Mayo Clinic sample was 97.5% White and from one US county; trial eligibility differs from licensed or clinical eligibility (UK labels differ, for example by ApoE4 status); CDR-SB and ARIA figures must be quoted exactly from Clarity AD.
scores.sharpen: Keep the funnel and add a plain reading of what the exclusions were (other illnesses, scan findings), closing with a question an older person can ask: would someone like me have been in the trial?

scores.accuracy_concern: The pilot had 60 families and a wait-list control; later, larger trials had mixed results that the core claim does not reflect; the NICE wording on tailored activities needs checking.
scores.sharpen: Either find and state the result of a larger Tailored Activity Program trial or reframe it as practical advice, clearly labelled, and consider merging its core point into C08-28.

scores.values_concern: Planning around reduced awareness should not become a reason to bypass the person; they still take part in decisions about their care.
scores.accuracy_concern: Reduced awareness is multifactorial (neurological, psychological, social), so 'comes from the illness itself' overstates a single mechanism; prevalence varies widely by method; the communication advice is carer guidance, not trial evidence, and must be labelled as such.
scores.sharpen: Say 'can come from the illness itself', give one verified prevalence range, and offer the task-based approach explicitly as practical advice.

scores.accuracy_concern: Nine men in one unit; the 25% and 84% increases are means from a tiny sample and invite overreading; replication has not been checked; the study size should appear in the first line.
scores.sharpen: Search for later replications; if none, drop the percentages from the visual and keep 'ate and drank more in a study of 9 people' with the 'try it and note intake before and after' instruction.

scores.values_concern: Avoid implying a position on Scottish Government policy or performance; state reach figures as facts.
scores.accuracy_concern: Public Health Scotland referral and completion percentages are unverified and the official publication may not be openable here; the estimated-cases denominator must be explained in plain words.
scores.sharpen: Lead with the entitlement for people in Scotland (a named link worker for at least a year) and add the verified reach figure with its denominator and year.

allocation_reason: 30 of 33 candidates reach 36 or more with no disqualifying flag and 22 reach 44 or more (note: the stated weights give a maximum of 55, not 50), so the category supports the 14 cap; weaker or out-of-scope items (C08-11, C08-14, C08-19, C08-20, C08-22, C08-23) could move to C09, C15, C17 or C19 if other categories need them.
balance_note: The top 14 (03, 15, 06, 24, 29, 17, 22, 08, 10, 25, 21, 27, 07, 28) split 3 practitioners, 5 both and 6 public, which is a good spread. Two imbalances: medicines take 5 of the 14 (03, 15, 17, 08, 07), and no Care that works post makes the top 14 while Reading the evidence has 5. Consider swapping 07 or 17 for C08-26 (WHELD) or C08-04 (mealtimes) to add good care and daily practice. Driving (19), money (20) and dementia in hospital (09) sit in scope but fall below the top 14, mainly because official UK pages could not be opened; 09 is the strongest of these and could replace 28 if hospital care is wanted.
